_comment: Registry of WordPress Credits student TRACKS, for the post-graduation tracker (#137).
WHY THIS IS DATA AND NOT CODE: more tracks are coming, and the plugin's Track Builder
(1.100.0) lets a program manager define one in the WordPress admin with an ARBITRARY
Learn course URL and an arbitrary track key. There is no slug naming convention to rely
on - 'wordpress-credits-designer' (no '-track' suffix) is an explicit example in the
plugin's own tests - and Track Builder stores its definitions as WordPress posts on the
dashboard site, which this Python job cannot read. So adding a track here is a one-line
data change with no code change, and scripts/post_grad_snapshot.py warns loudly when it
meets a track that is missing from this file (see the two canaries in that script).
WHEN A NEW TRACK LAUNCHES: add one entry to 'tracks' with the Learn course slug, the
track key the plugin uses (WPCPM_Program::track(), or the Track Builder 'key' field),
and the Airtable status name that students on the track carry while active. All three
come from the track's Track Builder definition.
The Learn course slug is the last path segment of the course URL, e.g.
'wordpress-credits-developer-track'. Completing a track course IS the graduation event.
This file holds no personal data: course slugs and status names only.

non_track_courses.wordpress-credits-mentors-course: Completed by mentors, not students. Counting it would invent graduates.

_non_track_statuses_comment: Airtable statuses that are NOT a track: a stage or a terminal state. Anything else in
the status field is treated as a track, which is the polarity that survives new tracks -
a track added in Airtable is automatically 'not one of these' and gets flagged if it is
missing from 'tracks' above. 'In Sensei Self-onboarding' is the 150h track's onboarding
stage, not a track of its own.
